Below is a non-exhaustive list of phrases that have been deployed—across everyday conversation, media, religion and political discourse—to stigmatize or marginalize LGBTQ+ people. Each entry includes a brief, academically oriented note on its negative implications.  

1. “That’s so gay”  
   • Equates “gay” with something undesirable, worthless or childish.  
   • Reinforces a stereotype that non-heterosexual identities are inferior or laughable.  

2. “No homo”  
   • A disclaimer that seeks to distance the speaker from any perceived same-sex attraction.  
   • Upholds heteronormativity and suggests that even joking about same-sex desire must be negated.  

3. “Faggot”  
   • A highly derogatory slur targeting gay men (and by extension, other gay or queer people).  
   • Dehumanizes, justifies exclusion or violence, and conveys that LGBTQ+ lives are contemptible.  

4. “Tranny”  
   • A pejorative term for transgender individuals.  
   • Invalidates trans identities, reduces them to a punch-line or spectacle, and contributes to social and physical vulnerability.  

5. “Homo”  
   • A clipped form of “homosexual” often used in a negative, mocking tone.  
   • Frames sexual orientation as deviant behavior rather than an intrinsic aspect of identity.  

6. “Alternative lifestyle”  
   • Implies that LGBTQ+ relationships and families are deviations from a presumed heterosexual “norm.”  
   • Pathologizes same-sex intimacy and gender diversity, suggesting they are elective or experimental.  

7. “Homosexual lifestyle”  
   • Reduces complex identities to a set of behaviors or choices.  
   • Suggests that coming out or same-sex relationships are optional “experiments,” rather than authentic self-expression.  

8. “Gay agenda”  
   • Conjures a conspiracy—that LGBTQ+ people secretly aim to undermine traditional values or institutions.  
   • Fuels moral panic, political opposition and the view of LGBTQ+ rights as an insidious threat.  

9. “Bathroom predator”  
   • Portrays transgender (or gender-nonconforming) people as dangerous intruders in sex-segregated spaces.  
   • Underlies discriminatory “bathroom bills” and contributes to harassment or violence.  

10. “It’s just a phase”  
    • Trivializes coming-out narratives or gender exploration by framing them as temporary fads.  
    • Invalidates lived experience and pressures individuals to conform to cis-heterosexual expectations.  

11. “Sex change”  
    • An outdated, sensationalizing term for gender-affirming surgery or transition.  
    • Conveys that trans identity is reducible to a single, “dramatic” medical event rather than an ongoing process of affirmation.  

12. “God doesn’t make mistakes”  
    • Invokes religious doctrine to label LGBTQ+ identities as unnatural or sinful.  
    • Justifies exclusion, “conversion” efforts or denial of equal rights on moral grounds.  

13. “Abomination”  
    • A moralistic condemnation (often drawn from specific religious texts) of same-sex intimacy or diverse gender expressions.  
    • Dehumanizes LGBTQ+ individuals, legitimizing discrimination as a form of “righteous” defense of societal purity.  

These phrases operate through various discursive strategies—slurs, pathologization, moral panic and conspiratorial framing—that collectively reinforce stigmas and legitimize exclusion or violence against LGBTQ+ people. Recognizing their function is a first step toward understanding and countering the broader social dynamics that sustain marginalization.
